discussion_comments.comment_body:
`fetch_secrets` only returns `nil` if the input is not a table. Since `upstream_ssl` here is an SSL object (table) obtained from `router.router_ssl.get_by_id()`, `fetch_secrets` will never return `nil`.

When a single secret query fails, the logic in `retrieve_refs` is `refs[k] = fetch(v, use_cache) or v`—that is, preserving the original `$secret://...` or `$env://...` string, instead of returning `nil`. This means:

- The `nil` check indicates the branch is unreachable, giving a false sense of security that "the error has been handled".

- The actual failure scenario (secret parsing failure, preserving an unparsed URI string) will not be intercepted and will be passed downstream, causing TLS handshake/decryption failures and generating incomprehensible error messages.

It is recommended to adopt a forgiving mode consistent with radixtree_sni.lua—remove nil checks and use `or upstream_ssl` for fallback.
